data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 explicitly detaches reliability from the checklist's content, but for objectively verifiable tasks the checklist encodes the decision rule linking observations to verifiable outcomes. A panel can have excellent social error-correction and full visible contestation, yet still answer incorrectly because the contested checklist item omits or misstates the objective criterion. The proposal offers no single-evaluation evidence that isolates the social correction effect from the checklist content; social visibility of disagreement does not distinguish whether the panel is reliably tracking the right answer or merely thoroughly executing the wrong checklist.
